title: 동네 · 이웃
intro: 집 주제와 짝으로 자주 나오는 단골 주제로, 동네 묘사 → 동네에서 하는 일 → 동네의 변화 → 어릴 때 동네와 비교 순서로 출제됩니다. 모든 답변은 '조용한 주거 지역, 지하철역 5분, 편의점·카페·작은 공원, 한강까지 자전거 10분'이라는 하나의 동네로 통일하세요. 공원 산책·한강 조깅·카페 공부 이야기가 그대로 공원·조깅·카페 주제 답변으로 재활용됩니다.
strategy: 답변 흐름: 'Sure, I'd love to talk about my neighborhood.' → 기본 정보(서울, 조용한 주거 지역, 10년째) → 주변 시설(지하철역·편의점·카페·공원·한강) → 내가 좋아하는 이유 → 'Yeah, that's ~' 마무리
'There's a ~ right next to ~', '~ is only five minutes away'로 거리와 위치를 구체적으로 말하세요.
변화·경험 질문은 예전 모습 → 무엇이 바뀌었는지 → 내 생활에 준 영향 → 느낌 순서로 과거시제와 현재를 대비시킵니다.
IH 이상은 사람·소리·계절 같은 생생한 디테일과 비교 표현(compared to, used to)을 더합니다.

expressions.en: Sure, I'd love to talk about my neighborhood.
expressions.ko: 네, 우리 동네에 대해 기꺼이 말씀드릴게요.

expressions.en: I live in a quiet residential area in Seoul.
expressions.ko: 저는 서울의 조용한 주거 지역에 살아요.

expressions.en: The subway station is only five minutes away on foot.
There's a convenience store right in front of my apartment.
expressions.ko: 우리 아파트 바로 앞에 편의점이 있어요.

expressions.en: There are a few nice cafes near my home.
expressions.ko: 집 근처에 괜찮은 카페가 몇 군데 있어요.

expressions.en: There's a small park where I like to take walks.
expressions.ko: 제가 산책하기 좋아하는 작은 공원이 있어요.

expressions.en: It only takes ten minutes to get to the Han River by bike.
What I like most about my neighborhood is that it's quiet but still convenient.
expressions.ko: 우리 동네에서 제일 좋은 점은 조용하면서도 편리하다는 거예요.
expressions.note: What I like most about ~ is that ~

expressions.en: The park used to be pretty run-down, but now it looks totally different.
expressions.ko: 공원이 예전엔 꽤 낡았는데, 지금은 완전히 달라졌어요.

expressions.en: Compared to the neighborhood I grew up in, this one is much more convenient.
expressions.ko: 제가 자란 동네에 비하면 여기가 훨씬 편리해요.
expressions.note: the neighborhood I grew up in

expressions.en: I often run into my neighbors at the convenience store.
So yeah, that's why I really like my neighborhood.
expressions.ko: 네, 그래서 저는 우리 동네가 정말 좋아요.

expressions.en: It's the kind of place where you can just walk out the door and find something to do.
expressions.ko: 문만 열고 나가면 할 게 있는 그런 동네예요.

expressions.en: After ten years here, I can't really picture myself living anywhere else.
expressions.ko: 여기서 10년을 살고 나니, 다른 데서 사는 건 잘 상상이 안 돼요.

questions.en: Tell me about your neighborhood. What does it look like, and what is there around your home?
questions.ko: 사는 동네에 대해 말해 주세요. 어떤 모습이고, 집 주변에는 무엇이 있나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 서울·조용한 주거 지역·10년째 → 지하철역·편의점·카페·공원·한강 → 좋아하는 이유 → 'Yeah, that's ~' 마무리
'There's a ~ right in front of ~', '~ minutes away'로 위치와 거리를 꼭 말하세요.
IH 이상은 저녁이나 주말의 동네 분위기(조용함, 산책하는 사람들)를 한 줄 넣으세요.

answers.IM3: Sure, I'd love to talk about my neighborhood. I live in a quiet residential area in Seoul. My family has lived here for about ten years. There are a lot of apartments and trees. The subway station is only five minutes away. There's a convenience store right in front of my apartment. There are also a few nice cafes and a small park. The Han River is just ten minutes away by bike. Yeah, that's why I really like my neighborhood.
answers.IH: Sure, I'd love to talk about my neighborhood. I live in a quiet residential area in Seoul, and my family has been here for about ten years. There are mostly apartment buildings, and the streets are lined with trees, so it looks really green in the summer. It's very convenient, too. The subway station is only five minutes away on foot, so getting to school is easy. There's a convenience store right in front of my apartment, and there are a few nice cafes nearby. I often go to one of them to study with an iced americano. There's also a small park where I like to take walks in the evening. And if I ride my bike for ten minutes, I can get to the Han River. What I like most about my neighborhood is that it's quiet but still convenient. Yeah, that's why I really like it here.
answers.AL: Sure, I'd love to talk about my neighborhood. I live in a quiet residential area in Seoul, and my family has been here for about ten years now, so I know pretty much every corner of it. It's mostly apartment buildings, but the streets are lined with big trees, so in the summer, the whole area feels green and peaceful. Even though it's quiet, it's surprisingly convenient. The subway station is only a five-minute walk away, which is a lifesaver on busy school days. There's a convenience store right in front of my building, and I'm there almost every night grabbing snacks. There are also a few cozy cafes nearby, and one of them has basically become my second study room. Then there's a small park just around the corner. In the evening, you see people walking their dogs, kids playing, and older couples chatting on the benches. And the best part is the Han River, which is only ten minutes away by bike. I go jogging there a few times a week, and the view at sunset is amazing. Honestly, it's the kind of place where you can just walk out the door and find something to do. Yeah, that's why I really love my neighborhood.

questions.en: What do you usually do in your neighborhood on weekends? Where do you go, and who do you go with?
questions.ko: 주말에 동네에서 보통 무엇을 하나요? 어디에 가고, 누구와 함께 가나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, my weekends? Let me think.' → 토요일 오전/오후/저녁 순서 → 장소(카페·공원·한강) + 함께하는 사람(Minji, 가족) → 느낌 → 'Yeah, that's ~' 마무리
공원 산책·한강 조깅·카페 공부 이야기는 공원·조깅·카페 주제에도 그대로 쓸 수 있어요.

answers.IM3: Oh, my weekends? Let me think. On Saturdays, I usually sleep in. In the afternoon, I meet my friend Minji at a cafe near my home. We drink iced americanos and study together. Sometimes we just talk for hours. In the evening, I take a walk in the small park with my mom. On Sundays, I ride my bike to the Han River and go jogging. It takes about ten minutes. Yeah, that's what I usually do on weekends.
answers.IH: Oh, my weekends? Let me think. Since my weekdays are pretty busy with classes, I like to keep my weekends relaxed. On Saturdays, I usually sleep in until ten. In the afternoon, I meet my best friend Minji at a cafe near my apartment. We order iced americanos and work on our assignments, but to be honest, we end up chatting most of the time. After that, we sometimes grab dinner at a small restaurant in the neighborhood. In the evening, I often take a walk in the park near my home with my mom. It's quiet and peaceful, so it's a nice way to end the day. On Sunday mornings, I ride my bike to the Han River, which takes about ten minutes, and go jogging for half an hour. It really helps me get ready for the new week. Yeah, that's pretty much my weekend.
answers.AL: Oh, my weekends? Let me think. My weekdays are packed with classes, so on weekends, I try to slow things down and just enjoy my neighborhood. On Saturdays, I let myself sleep in until about ten, which feels like the best luxury in the world. In the afternoon, I usually meet my best friend Minji at a little cafe around the corner from my apartment. The plan is always to study, so we order iced americanos and open our laptops, but somehow we end up talking for two hours straight. If we're hungry afterward, we grab dinner at one of the small restaurants nearby. Later in the evening, I often take a walk in the park near my home with my mom. It's our little catch-up time, since we barely see each other during the week. Sunday mornings are for exercise. I hop on my bike, ride about ten minutes to the Han River, and go jogging along the river for half an hour. The air is fresh, there are tons of people out cycling, and it honestly clears my head for the week ahead. It's nothing fancy, but I love how I can do all of this without leaving my neighborhood. Yeah, that's what my weekends usually look like.

questions.en: Has your neighborhood changed since you first moved there? Tell me about a memorable change. What happened, and how did it affect you?
questions.ko: 처음 이사 왔을 때와 비교해 동네가 변했나요? 기억에 남는 변화에 대해 말해 주세요. 무슨 일이 있었고, 그것이 당신에게 어떤 영향을 주었나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, changes in my neighborhood? Let me think.' → 예전 모습 → 언제·무엇이 바뀌었는지 → 내 생활의 변화 → 느낌 → 'Yeah, that's ~' 마무리
'used to + 동사원형'(예전) vs. 'Now, ~'(지금) 대비로 변화를 보여 주세요.
IH 이상은 변화가 내 일상(산책, 조깅, 공부)에 준 구체적 영향을 꼭 말하세요.

answers.IM3: Oh, changes in my neighborhood? Let me think. Yes, my neighborhood changed a lot. The small park near my home used to be old and dark. There were only a few benches. About two years ago, the city fixed the park. Now it has a walking path, new benches, and lots of flowers. It's also bright at night. So I started taking walks there every evening. I really like it. Yeah, that's the biggest change in my neighborhood.
answers.IH: Oh, changes in my neighborhood? Let me think. When we first moved here about ten years ago, the small park near my apartment was pretty run-down. There were a few old benches and some broken lights, so it was too dark to go there at night. About two years ago, the city renovated the whole park. It took about six months, and there was a lot of noise, so it was a little annoying. But when it opened again, it looked totally different. Now there's a nice walking path, new benches, and lots of flowers and trees. There are bright lights, so it feels safe at night. Since then, I've been taking walks there almost every evening. Sometimes I go with my mom, and sometimes I just listen to music alone. Yeah, that's the most memorable change in my neighborhood.
answers.AL: Oh, changes in my neighborhood? Let me think. Actually, the biggest change happened to the small park right near my apartment. When my family first moved here about ten years ago, that park was pretty run-down. There were a couple of old benches, the playground was rusty, and half the lights didn't work, so nobody really went there after dark. Then about two years ago, the city decided to renovate the whole thing. For about six months, there was construction noise every morning, and to be honest, it drove me a little crazy, especially during exam season. But when the park finally reopened, I could hardly believe it was the same place. Now there's a smooth walking path that loops around the park, new benches under the trees, and flowers everywhere in the spring. They also put in bright lights, so it feels safe even late at night. That change really affected my daily life. I started taking walks there almost every evening, sometimes with my mom and sometimes alone with my earphones in. It's become my favorite place to clear my head after a long day of classes. Looking back, those six months of noise were totally worth it. Yeah, that's the most memorable change in my neighborhood.

questions.en: How is the neighborhood you live in now different from the one you grew up in?
questions.ko: 지금 사는 동네는 어린 시절을 보낸 동네와 어떻게 다른가요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, the neighborhood I grew up in? Let me think.' → 예전 동네 소개 → 지금 동네와 다른 점 2~3개 → 어느 쪽이 좋은지와 이유 → 'Yeah, that's ~' 마무리
'Compared to ~', 'used to', 'much more convenient'로 비교를 분명하게 하세요.
집 주제와 맞춰 '10년 전쯤 초등학생 때 서울의 다른 동네에서 이사 왔다'로 통일하세요.

answers.IM3: Oh, the neighborhood I grew up in? Let me think. When I was a child, I lived in an old neighborhood in a different part of Seoul. There were many small houses and narrow streets. There was a big traditional market, so it was always noisy. But the subway station was far away. My neighborhood now is quiet and clean. The subway station is only five minutes away. There's also a park and the Han River nearby. Yeah, I like my neighborhood now better.
answers.IH: Oh, the neighborhood I grew up in? Let me think. Until I was in elementary school, my family lived in an old neighborhood in a different part of Seoul. There were lots of small houses and narrow streets, and there was a big traditional market nearby. It was always busy and a little noisy, but everyone knew each other. The problem was that the subway station was about 20 minutes away on foot. About ten years ago, we moved to the neighborhood I live in now, and it's really different. It's a quiet residential area with lots of apartments and trees. Compared to my old neighborhood, it's much more convenient. The subway station is only five minutes away, and there are cafes, a park, and even the Han River nearby. I do miss the friendly market people sometimes. But overall, I like my neighborhood now much better. Yeah, that's the biggest difference.
answers.AL: Oh, the neighborhood I grew up in? Let me think. Until I was in elementary school, my family lived in an old neighborhood in a different part of Seoul, and it had a totally different vibe. It was full of small houses and narrow, winding streets, and right in the middle, there was a huge traditional market. From early in the morning, you could hear the shop owners calling out to customers, and the whole street smelled like fried snacks. It was noisy, but it had a really warm feeling, because everyone knew each other. My mom couldn't buy groceries without stopping to chat with three neighbors. The downside was that it wasn't very convenient. The nearest subway station was about a 20-minute walk away, and there weren't many parks. About ten years ago, we moved to the neighborhood I live in now, and the difference was huge. It's a quiet residential area with tall apartment buildings and tree-lined streets. Compared to my old neighborhood, it's way more convenient, with a subway station five minutes away, cozy cafes, a nice park, and the Han River just a short bike ride away. I'll admit it's a bit less lively, and I sometimes miss the market. But for a busy college student like me, I wouldn't trade it for anything. Yeah, that's how the two neighborhoods are different.

pronunciation.tip: '네이버후드'. 첫 음절 '네이'에 강세, gh는 소리 없음
첫 음절 '레'에 강세. '레너베이티드', t는 부드럽게 굴려도 OK
